verdict.rationale: Pricing stability is a fair question for a commercial game engine, so the axis applies. The pack shows the opposite of a stable track record: community reports describe the per-install Runtime Fee announcement and a unilateral forced move to a more expensive license, and the only first-party item is a blog post titled 'Unity is Canceling the Runtime Fee', which shows a reversal rather than any documented commitment against retroactive repricing. No first-party policy guaranteeing license-term stability appears in the evidence.

support.subject: As a studio lead, the pricing and license terms have a track record of stability — no retroactive changes that reprice games already shipped
